candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XLV.4. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live?' Ephrem reads the self-revelation as the model of merciful self-disclosure: the brothers, expecting wrath, hear MERCY first. Tewahedo theological-anthropology preserves this pattern: divine self-disclosure in Christ runs ahead of and overwhelms human expectation of judgment. The risen Christ's 'Peace be unto you' to the apostles who abandoned Him is the Joseph-pattern fulfilled.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life'. Tewahedo providence-theology (especially developed in monastic spiritual direction for those processing past harms) draws on Gen 45:5: the harm was real; God's purpose ran deeper than the harm.
